newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus students protest to mark human rights day.
newsitem.headline: Belarus students protest to mark human rights day.

text.p: Hundreds of students protested at hardline President Alexander Lukashenko's policies in Belarus on Tuesday to mark International Human Rights day.
They gathered on a central avenue in the capital to demand the release of fellow opponents of Lukashenko arrested at previous demonstrations, some of which erupted in clashes.
Lukashenko has been criticised by the West for using a huge victory in a November 24 referendum to rewrite the constitution and grant himself sweeping powers.
"Political repressions are going on in Belarus. We demand freedom and the release of all politicial prisoners," student Alexei Yankevich said.
Police imposed $15 fines on dozens of students bearing portraits of Slavomir Adamovich, who wrote a poem entitled "Kill the president" and has been held without trial for nine months.

"Adamovich was outlawed for provoking terror. Apart from poems, a weapon was confiscated -- a gas pistol. He faces three years' prison," First Deputy General Prosecutor Vladimir Kondratyev told Reuters.
The protesters were also demanding the release of seven nationalists from neighbouring Ukraine who are serving prison sentences of between 18 months and 2-1/2 years.
They were accused of provoking violence at a huge protest in Minsk last April at which demonstrators clashed with police, leading to more than 200 arrests.
The protestors also demanded a pardon for Andrei Romashevsky, leader of the Beer Lovers' Party.

He is serving a 2-1/2- year suspended sentence for hanging a hammer and sickle from a public toilet near Lukashenko's administration to protest at his policy of rebuilding a union with Russia and his nostalgia for the Soviet past.
Lukashenko has attracted widespread criticism from human rights bodies and the West for muzzling the media and ignoring the constitution.
